title: Meta-Learned Metrics over Multi-Evolution Temporal Graphs

problem.claim: Graph metric learning aims to learn distances that bring similar graphs closer and dissimilar graphs farther apart for graph classification.

gap.claim: Most graph metric learning methods treat graphs as static and ignore the heterogeneous dynamics of temporal graphs.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Temp-GFSM, a temporal graph metric learning framework.
Temp-GFSM models evolving patterns, weighs them to represent temporal-class characteristics, and learns a metric using few labels.
With few labeled temporal graphs, Temp-GFSM can classify temporal graphs and adapt to discover subspaces for unseen classes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world temporal graph classification tasks from various domains report that Temp-GFSM is effective.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph metric learning seeks distances that separate similar and dissimilar graphs and supports graph classification applications.
Existing methods largely ignore temporal and heterogeneous graph dynamics, while temporal-graph labeling is expensive and requires background knowledge.
The paper proposes Temp-GFSM to learn metrics over temporal graphs from few labels by modeling and weighting evolving patterns.
The framework is described as supporting temporal-graph classification and adaptation to unseen classes with few labeled examples.
Experiments on real-world temporal graph classification tasks across domains report effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: Temporal graphs may contain heterogeneous microscopic and macroscopic evolution patterns.

interpretation.claim: A useful temporal-graph representation may need to account for multiple scales or types of evolution.

application.claim: When designing temporal graph metrics, model and weight evolving patterns according to their relevance to temporal classes.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this strategy is necessary or effective for every temporal graph task.

source_observation.claim: Labeling temporal graphs is described as expensive and dependent on background knowledge.

interpretation.claim: Few-label learning is a relevant design constraint for temporal graph classification.

application.claim: Evaluate temporal graph methods under limited-label conditions when annotation costs are high.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how few labels are defined or how performance changes with label availability.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide dataset names, task counts, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The details of Temp-GFSM's components and training procedure are unspecified.
The number of labeled temporal graphs and the unseen-class adaptation protocol are unspecified.
